name: Agent Sentinel

card.question: Can we trust what the agent did?
card.title: Agent Sentinel: a flight recorder for AI agents
card.description: Built for regulated firms: every finding links a rule a person wrote, the action that broke it and the evidence, mapped to DORA, EU AI Act and CSSF controls. Open code and tests behind each part. Start with Part 1.
card.audience: CISOs, risk and compliance teams, auditors, and the architects putting AI agents into regulated work.

inShort.1: Most firms running AI agents have logs, not evidence. Agent Sentinel records what each agent did, checks it against rules people wrote, and turns anything outside them into a finding an auditor can check: which agent, which rule, what evidence.
inShort.2: A monitoring tool that can break a payments run gets switched off. The rule here: if the recorder fails, the agent must not, and lost evidence is counted, never silent. Testing my own code against that rule found five gaps; each now has a test.
inShort.3: An auditor can check a rule, not a score of 0.87. Written rules decide every finding; a pattern model may only advise, can never overrule a rule, and ships switched off. Two-thirds of the code contains no AI at all.
inShort.4: A tool that holds evidence must pass a bank’s security review first: who can call it, where the data lives, who looked at what, and whether a risky finding waits for a person. This part answers each question and lists what isn’t done yet.
inShort.5: Security teams don’t need another screen. Each finding goes, already explained, into the SIEM they use. Blocking stays on the roadmap; when it comes, written rules, not statistics, will decide what is blocked.
inShort.6: Agent Sentinel doesn’t read prompts to spot attacks; it checks what the agent did next. Against ten outcomes of one injected invoice, it caught every action outside the agent’s policy and none inside it. The policy is the control.
inShort.7: A recorder is a data platform that holds evidence, so a lost row is a gap in the evidence. Events are saved before any rule runs, only a redacted preview is kept, and a storage backend that can’t keep an audit trail refuses instead of pretending.
